messages.content: Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has four participants with equal initial private endowments. Each makes one allocation to a Group Account, choosing any whole number of ECUs from zero to their endowment. Each ECU allocated costs its contributor one private ECU and generates the stated per-person return for EACH of all four group members, including its contributor. Final allocation earnings equal the private endowment minus own allocation plus the per-person return times the sum of all four allocations. The estimate concerns the average allocation of the OTHER THREE members, excluding the person’s own allocation. In this version each person gives the estimate first and allocates second. The others’ current choices and allocation earnings have not been revealed at either decision. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

This is UK general population online Prolific. Each of the four members, including this person, starts with 100 ECUs. The return to EACH member is 0.8 ECU per ECU put into the Group Account. No age, gender, or other personal attributes are supplied in these records. What mean amount does this person estimate for the OTHER THREE group members’ Group Account allocations? Give the estimate in ECUs.

Each ECU allocated costs its contributor one private ECU and generates the stated per-person return for EACH of all four group members, including its contributor. Final allocation earnings equal the private endowment minus own allocation plus the per-person return times the sum of all four allocations. The estimate concerns the average allocation of the OTHER THREE members, excluding the person’s own allocation. In this version each person gives the estimate first and allocates second. The others’ current choices and allocation earnings have not been revealed at either decision. Every 100 ECUs convert to €2, in addition to a €2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to €1.5: participants are told this is €1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at €1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns €0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each ECU allocated costs its contributor one private ECU and generates the stated per-person return for EACH of all four group members, including its contributor. Final allocation earnings equal the private endowment minus own allocation plus the per-person return times the sum of all four allocations. The estimate concerns the average allocation of the OTHER THREE members, excluding the person’s own allocation. In this version each person gives the estimate first and allocates second. The others’ current choices and allocation earnings have not been revealed at either decision. Every 100 ECUs convert to €2, in addition to a €2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to €1.5: participants are told this is €1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at €1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns €0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Each ECU allocated costs its contributor one private ECU and generates the stated per-person return for EACH of all four group members, including its contributor. Final allocation earnings equal the private endowment minus own allocation plus the per-person return times the sum of all four allocations. The estimate concerns the average allocation of the OTHER THREE members, excluding the person’s own allocation. In this version each person allocates first and gives the estimate second. The others’ current choices and allocation earnings have not been revealed at either decision. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the THRESHOLD mechanism: the public return starts at 0.4 per contributed ECU for each member. If the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total at least 100 ECUs, the return becomes 0.8; only 100 ECUs are spent and offers above 100 are refunded in proportion to each beneficiary’s gross offer. If the offers total less than 100, the return stays 0.4 and ALL offers are refunded. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Beneficiaries make no allocation and keep their initial private budget plus the public return on provider allocations. Providers estimate the mean Group Account allocation of the OTHER THREE providers before making their own allocation. Beneficiaries give an estimate of the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers; they have no transfer decision. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Beneficiaries make no allocation and keep their initial private budget plus the public return on provider allocations. Providers estimate the mean Group Account allocation of the OTHER THREE providers before making their own allocation. Beneficiaries give an estimate of the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers; they have no transfer decision. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Beneficiaries make no allocation and keep their initial private budget plus the public return on provider allocations. Providers estimate the mean Group Account allocation of the OTHER THREE providers before making their own allocation. Beneficiaries give an estimate of the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers; they have no transfer decision. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. The public return is fixed by the treatment. All offered transfers are split equally among the four providers, regardless of their contributions. This is additional income and does not increase a provider’s allocation limit of 100. A beneficiary earns their private budget minus own transfer plus their public-goods return; a provider also receives one quarter of the transfer total. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the gross Transfer Account offer in whole ECUs. Return only the number; do not output the eventual net cost or refund.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the THRESHOLD mechanism: the public return starts at 0.4 per contributed ECU for each member. If the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total at least 100 ECUs, the return becomes 0.8; only 100 ECUs are spent and offers above 100 are refunded in proportion to each beneficiary’s gross offer. If the offers total less than 100, the return stays 0.4 and ALL offers are refunded. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the Group Account allocation in whole ECUs. Return only the number, not a percentage of endowment or total group allocation.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the THRESHOLD mechanism: the public return starts at 0.4 per contributed ECU for each member. If the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total at least 100 ECUs, the return becomes 0.8; only 100 ECUs are spent and offers above 100 are refunded in proportion to each beneficiary’s gross offer. If the offers total less than 100, the return stays 0.4 and ALL offers are refunded. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

If the offers total less than 100, the return stays 0.4 and ALL offers are refunded. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.

Predict the participant’s actual response in an anonymous, randomly matched, one-time public-goods experiment. There is no repeated interaction and no communication. An ECU is an experimental currency unit. The group has eight participants: four Type 1 beneficiaries and four Type 2 providers. Everyone reads the treatment rules and passes comprehension questions before learning their randomly assigned type. Each provider makes one allocation from their private endowment of 100 ECUs to a Group Account, in whole ECUs from 0 to 100. Each contributed ECU generates the stated public return for EACH of all eight members, including its contributor. A provider’s public-goods earnings are 100 minus own allocation plus this return times the sum of the FOUR provider allocations. Each beneficiary first estimates the mean Group Account allocation of ALL FOUR providers, then independently offers a whole-number transfer from zero to their own private budget to a Transfer Account. Beneficiaries choose before providers act and do not see the other beneficiaries’ current offers. Providers first estimate the mean gross Transfer Account offer of ALL FOUR beneficiaries. This is an estimate about the other type, not about the other providers. Only AFTER this estimate does a provider see the actual total offered to the Transfer Account and its public-return value, then choose their Group Account allocation. This is the CONTINUOUS mechanism: if the four beneficiaries’ gross offers total S ECUs, the public return per contributed ECU for EACH member is 0.4 + 0.004 × min(S, 100), with a maximum of 0.8. If S exceeds 100, the excess is refunded to beneficiaries in proportion to their gross offers; otherwise there is no refund. A beneficiary earns the private budget minus the gross offer plus any refund plus the public-goods return. Providers receive no cash transfer income. Provider allocations are made independently; other providers’ current choices and resulting public-goods earnings are not revealed before these decisions. Every 100 ECUs convert to £2, in addition to a £2 participation payment. The estimate can earn a separate bonus up to £1.5: participants are told this is £1.5 divided by the absolute ECU difference between their estimate and the actual average, capped at £1.5; an error of 10 ECUs earns £0.15. Final earnings are processed after everyone finishes. Predict the numerical estimate in ECUs. Return only the number; it is a subjective estimate, not the actual group average.
